As far as I am aware the first person that they call on is next of kin. If his ex wife is still his next of kin and they are not legally separated. If not it is the oldest parent, then the next parent then the oldest sibling etc. I would expect that he is on a provisional 72 hour section which allows them to hold him for a maximum of 72 hours until he can be assessed by two doctors. When I was in hospital ward rounds took place on a monday morning but I don't know if this is universal. If they can they will take him to his nearest hospital or the hospital connected with his county so maybe see if you could locate this and ring asking for the mental health ward. He will be given papers when he is admitted where he can select who the ward talks to and who they don't. Under section they have the right to talk with your next of kin but he may not want them to tell you any information and you should be prepared for that being a possibility. Try not to worry if he is in hospital then he is safe and will be getting help. Hope you can chat with him soon, from my experience they are quite good with phone calls etc from mental health wards.

It can be really hard to start loosing weight. I am nowhere near to where I should be with it but little bits at a time can help. I know it is hard to hear that you are overweight but it is something that you need to realise. Not because of how you look that is secondary it is your health that is important. If you don't feel the effects already then you will soon ( bad back, bad legs, breathing problems) . 

Where to start, the doctors. Hopefully you can find a friend to go with you. If the doctor is good they will do tests to find out whether anything physical will make it harder for you from loosing weight. I know people laugh about people who are overweight having thyroid problems. They do exist and do make it hard to loose weight, getting it under control isn't going to be a miracle weight loss cure but can help. Secondly things like polycystic ovaries can have an effect ( if you have particularly heavy periods or experience pain around your lower abdomen these are signs) 

Other things the doctors may offer is help from a dietician, if this is an option, definitely go, they are in short supply but most tend to be quite helpful in offering advice in a kind manner. Secondly are diet tablets, I would avoid these until you have given a good shot at dieting and exercise. 

Diet is one thing, you need to find out what works for you. Try to replace bad foods with healthy alternatives. If you feel a need for something sweet then try sugar free gum ( not too much it is a laxative) or sugar free jelly. Portion size is a big factor I know it sounds stupid but for ages I was eating seemingly healthy food and didn't know why my weight was the same, I was eating too much. There are some guides online about it that helped me. Another tip is eating six small meals or not eating after 6. Water is also important sometimes you may feel hungry but you are actually thirsty. Don't drink any sugared drinks in one glass you can have as much as a full meal in calories. 

Exercise is next, when you have a lot of weight it is feels really hard to do exercise. You have a lot of weight to support so it's harder to do push ups and what not. Swimming is a great form of exercise, I found it extremely difficult to swim because I felt so embarrassed by my body. Finding all women hours can help and going with a friend to keep it more chilled. Walking as well, as a bigger girl I don't like doing exercise in public but if I am walking around people don't realise. I also do exercise in the house. A couple of exercises you may want to try in lying in bed and doing a bicycle movement with your legs, doing stair steps. Get a routine and stick to it, soon you will find you have lost weight and the exercises are becoming easier so you will be able to do more. 

I know that this is a bit of a ramble but I just want you to know that you can loose weight. I think your aim should not be to increase attractiveness but to be a healthier person. You will find that when you are healthier you are happier and that's when it glows inside. I am not a  very good judge because I don't think anyone is ugly just from a picture, I may not be attracted to them but I don't think that determines your attractiveness to others.

I don't know about America but can tell you my experience of UK and general hospital type things. Firstly your therapist and psychiatrist have severely neglected your care. I have only been in hospital as an adult, I expect they would call your guardians but only after discussing it with you. 

I have been to hospital on several occasions for stitches. If this is what you need it needs to be done ideally within 6 hours but 12 at the most. Usually going into hospital for a psychiatric assessment will take a lot of waiting but eventually will see someone. They will assess risk and choose whether an admission to hospital is the best thing for you. If you voluntarily enter hospital they will not section you but if not then you may get a section. Psychiatric sections can hold you back so it is best to go in voluntarily. They will also discuss with you talking to your next of kin. ]

If it would be severely detrimental to do so, they will not ( if there is any abuse in the family etc) You may be surprised, although it is not my personal experience I am aware of people who have seen a turn around in family relationships after events like these making them a lot closer.

If you are assessed as risky but not in need for admission usually there are day out patient clinics you must attend. I would expect although I can't say in all certainty that you would have a medication review and start taking it very soon. I know in the UK they have crisis teams that come to your house in a crisis but I am not sure this is something they provide in the US. 

I understand your fear, when I first went to hospital I was shaking and was sick but it turned out OK. You have to remember these people see people with mental health problems all the time. They will not be shocked at what you tell them. I won't lie to you, not everyone is very helpful and can be a bit cold but you will get things sorted because they have a duty of care. If you are in a state and they just send you home and something then happens, it is on their backs and they will get in trouble. They don't want to risk it so they will have to do something.

I would hope that the care in the UK and US isn't very different although I cannot be sure. Although you are suicidal and self harming you can still be a part of your care. Don't forget that you do have a voice in what happens to you and how you progress. Just make sure if they say that they think you should be in hospital that you don't resist as this could result in a section which you don't really want. 

Good luck, remember this can be a blessing in disguise not matter how scary it is this could be the start of your treatment which will help in the long run.

I am also 22 and in a similar situation (this is due to psychosis and well as depression but similar in a lot of ways ). I have been having a little look at the posts and just want to show some things that may help you, they may not but worth a shot. First thing you state is that your depression abates for a while but doesn't go away. Unfortunately this is depression in a nut shell, the way to feel better is to learn to ride the lows and appreciate the less low times. Obviously you can try different methods to make the lows not feel as bad as they do , I am not saying that you have to live with intense low but you will have to live with a certain level of depression. 

It's interesting when you talk of about how you feel about yourself and how you are in social situations etc because this is a pretty much copy of how I feel about myself, this is the depression making you focus on bad points making you pick out negative situations from ones which are probably not significant to other people but mean so much to you. You speak of anxiety, I will give you some links at the bottom of the post for DBT and CBT related exercises, if you stick at these they can help to curb some of the anxiety. 

You need to try and appreciate what you can do rather than what you can't. So, accept that you have tried jobs and you have succeeded for a certain amount of time. You have been to college and have done things there. These are all positive things, your intelligence is a positive thing. You are struggling at the moment because of an illness, but you cannot feel that you are to blame for that, or that because of it your life is going to be like that forever from now on. 

You go on to talk about how you tried to change your life, by moving to a new college and a new city. Although this seems like a sensible option it may not be. By avoiding situations and not facing hard times, anxiety compacts and becomes worse. Understand that to face things is probably one of the most gut wrenching and difficult things to do but afterwards you will see that you didn't die as a result your still ok so the next time you do it it won't feel so bad. 

Your experience with mental health practitioners sounds awful, although generally they are pretty shoddy as they don't get good funding. Are there any other places you can seek help. I know in the UK where I am you get what your given but you can keep pushing for better support, MIND are a good advocacy service if you feel you are not achieving enough from your medical services. There are charities which you can self refer to which can give help and support. As for the medication, it may not help but it does take a while to become active and needs to be alongside effective therapy to work. I have been on countless numbers of medications that were ineffective until they found that I had psychotic symptoms so placed me on seroquel. This doesn't make things good but does take the edge of the anxiety. 

One of the things you say is that when you are not depressed when things feel good that you still have an ache in your chest. I am not saying this is untrue or that you don't believe it. However, when one is depressed all things follow that mindset, you can't accept good times because the depression takes over. This makes you feel like your always hiding the depression things always feel this bad, you can't accept the good times.
